fields.meta_title: Payroll Automation for Hourly Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Four payroll automation examples for hourly teams: overtime review, hours checks, raise approvals, and cutoff reminders. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Payroll Automation Around Your Payroll Provider
fields.hero_description: Build payroll automation that checks every timesheet and holds unusual hours before the payroll cutoff.
fields.features_heading: The Payroll Work That Happens Before the Run
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the app that collects hours and pay changes, then hands them to the payroll provider you already use.
fields.feature_1:
One timesheet flow for every store

Hourly staff submit their week from a phone, and each timesheet lands with the manager who owns that store. Overtime and missing days are marked before anyone opens payroll.
fields.feature_2:
Checks you write in plain English

Type a rule such as "hold anyone whose hours jump by a quarter" and Emergent builds the check along with the database that stores each result. To change the rule, prompt again.
fields.feature_3:
Rate changes with a named approver

Raises and shift premiums move through the approvers you set, with the old rate and the new rate side by side. Payroll only receives a change after its approver says yes.
fields.feature_4:
Connected to your payroll provider

If your time clock and payroll provider have APIs, the app reads hours from one and sends approved rates to the other. Books in QuickBooks or Xero connect the same way.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders that reach a person

Slack, email, and in-app alerts go to the manager who owns each open timesheet, timed against the payroll cutoff you set. An escalation goes to the next person you name.
fields.feature_6:
Every pay period on record

Each timesheet and each approval is saved with a name and a time in a database you own. A live dashboard shows what is still open before the cutoff for this pay period.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Payroll Automations to Build First
fields.tab_content_1:
A 46-hour week waits for its manager

Ines Valdovinos submits a 46-hour week from the Eastgate store of Corvell Bakery. Corvell's rule counts hours past 40 in a week as overtime, and the app marks 6 overtime hours before it sends the timesheet to her manager, Teodor Sandberg. He approves it in the app, and her week is ready for payroll.
fields.tab_content_2:
Hours up by half on last period wait for review

Before the pay run, the app lines up each person's approved hours against the last period. Dariusz Lemaire shows 72 hours against 48, up by half. Corvell holds any change over 25%. His line waits for Mireille Okafor, the payroll lead, with both timesheets attached, while every other line stays ready.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any raise over 5% needs the HR director

Hamid Rasuli's store manager requests a raise from $18.00 to $19.50 an hour, up more than 8%. Raises up to 5% go through on the manager's request alone. This one waits for Saoirse Kettering, the HR director. Once she approves, the app writes the new rate to the payroll provider through its API.
fields.tab_content_4:
Two days out, each manager sees what is still open

Corvell's payroll cutoff is Thursday at 5 p.m. On Tuesday the app finds 3 unapproved timesheets at the Riverside store, from Lucan Ferreira, Yusra Haddad, and Pia Lindqvist. Their manager, Odalys Brennan, gets a direct message that lists all 3 with one button to open them.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan payroll automation around your pay calendar, then build and test it with Emergent before it goes live.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write each rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Connect the time clock and provider
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the calendar and the cutoff
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every manual step between the time clock and payday: who collects hours, who approves them, and who keys in rate changes. Mark each place where someone copies a number from one screen to another. Those go first.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write each rule the way you would explain it to a new payroll clerk. A timesheet missing a scheduled shift goes back to the employee, and a new shift premium needs the operations lead. Emergent builds the app and its logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect the time clock and the payroll provider through their APIs. Decide which system owns each fact: hours come from the clock, and pay rates come from the provider. Nobody should keep a second copy in a spreadsheet.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Enter the pay dates and the cutoff for each period. Pick when reminders go out and who hears about a timesheet that is still open after the last reminder. Name one person per store, not a shared channel.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose what a person must approve
fields.howto_step_5_des: Mark the changes that alter someone's pay: overtime, raises, back pay, and a final paycheck. Each one should wait for a named approver who sees the old figure next to the new one before anything reaches payroll.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run the last two pay periods through the app before it touches a live run. Compare its approved hours and rates with what payroll paid, line by line. Fix any rule that disagrees by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live with one store first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Switch on one location for a full pay period while the others stay on the old process. Count the corrections payroll had to make after the cutoff, then add the next location once that count reaches zero.

faq_plan.a: Payroll automation is the use of software to perform the routine payment and compliance tasks of payroll: time tracking, wage calculation, benefits, tax withholding, and direct deposit. The software turns hours and pay rates into paychecks and schedules each deposit for payday.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up payroll automation?
faq_plan.a: Describe the work around your pay run in Emergent's AI automation builder, one rule per sentence. Say who submits hours and which changes need an approver before the cutoff. Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard, and connects it to any system you name that offers an API.

faq_plan.q: Is there a way to automate payroll?
faq_plan.ref: Is there a way to automate payroll?

prov.original: Is there a way to automate payroll?

faq_plan.a: Yes. Payroll software calculates wages, withholds federal, state, and local taxes, and schedules direct deposits for payday. The inputs still need people: someone confirms the hours and approves a raise before the run. Those checks and approvals can be automated as well, around the provider you already pay.

faq_plan.q: What should payroll automation software include?
faq_plan.a: It should include connections to the time clock that records hours, the HR system that holds pay rates, and the accounting tool that books each run. Every handoff left manual is a number someone retypes. The same pattern, with inputs checked before a named approver signs off, runs an automated loan processing system, where applications take the place of timesheets.

faq_plan.q: Which payroll decisions should an automated payroll system not automate?
faq_plan.a: Leave the judgment calls to people: whether a 60-hour week happened, whether a raise was promised, and what a final paycheck should include. Write down who decides each one, and give that person a deadline ahead of the cutoff.

faq_plan.q: Which steps of automated payroll processing should I automate first?
faq_plan.a: Start with timesheet approvals and the reminders before the cutoff. They repeat every period and change no pay rate. A mistake there costs a reminder, not a paycheck. Emergent sets no task cap, and a period full of extra shifts runs the same as a quiet one.

faq_plan.q: Can I use automated payroll software for contractor invoices?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if your provider pays contractors. ADP's RUN platform, for one, runs payments for W-2 employees and 1099 contractors in the same platform. The contractor's invoice still needs approval before it is paid. That approval step is where invoice automation fits: the invoice is read into fields, checked against the agreed rate, and routed to the person who signs off.

faq_plan.q: Do automated payroll services include pay stubs and year-end tax forms?
faq_plan.a: Pay stubs, yes: automated payroll tools keep post-payroll records such as pay stubs and reports. Year-end tax forms depend on the provider, and some go further by generating W-2s or 1099s. Before you sign, ask which forms yours produces and how far back it keeps each record.

faq_plan.q: What should I test before I use an automated payroll service?
faq_plan.a: Run one pay period through both the old process and the new automated payroll service, then compare net pay for every person, line by line. Confirm that year-to-date totals and every deduction carried over. Timesheets and approvals in an app built with Emergent sit in a database you own, and they stay put when the provider changes.

faq_plan.q: What does the payroll automation process include each pay period?
faq_plan.a: Each period, the payroll automation process includes four stages: hours come in from the time clock, managers approve them, payroll reviews anything held, and the provider runs pay after the cutoff. After payday, report automation can send finance a summary of hours and cost by store.

findings.quote: No, not when contractors bill you. A contractor's invoice is a bill, and it belongs with your other bills.
findings.issue: FAQ 7 ('Can I use automated payroll software for contractor invoices?') gives a flat 'No' about what payroll software can do, with no domain source. Many payroll providers pay contractors and file their 1099s, and this page's own FAQ 8 says 'some go further by generating W-2s or 1099s', so the page contradicts itself. This is the only instance of the class; the other third-party facts (Oyster definition and post-payroll records, Workday tax withholding) match their quoted spans.
findings.fix: Answer what is true: many payroll providers can pay contractors and prepare 1099s (source it), but an invoice a contractor sends still needs checking against the agreed rate and an approval, which is where invoice automation fits. Keep the link; drop the flat 'No'.
